question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Times at Which a Particle Is Stationary
question.problem:
A particle $P$ moves in the $x$-$y$ plane (relative to a fixed origin $O$) with position vector

$$
r=⟨{t}^{2}-6t,(t-3)^{5}⟩,\,t\in [0,\infty ).
$$

Calculate the times at which the particle is stationary.
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-6t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t-3)^{5})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t-6,5(t-3)^{4}⟩ \\  & =⟨2(t-3),5(t-3)^{4}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The particle is stationary when its velocity is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =0 \\ ⟨2(t-3),5(t-3)^{4}⟩ & =⟨0,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So we need

$$
\begin{aligned}2(t-3)=0\, & ⇒\,t=3, \\ 5(t-3)^{4}=0\, & ⇒\,t=3.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $t=3$ is the only solution that satisfies both equations, so this is the only value of $t$ when the particle is stationary.
